subject: Edge-onprem bootstrap: tenant locality, mixed-node profiles & encrypted blockstore plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@warehousesys.com>, Ops Eng <ops@warehousesys.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Edge-onprem bootstrap: tenant locality, mixed-node profiles & encrypted blockstore plan

Janet / Warehouse Systems team —

Thanks for the time last week. Per our conversation, we put together an initial bootstrap plan for the on-prem/private deployment that focuses on three things we heard were high priority: tenant locality (data residency per floor/rack), a mixed-node profile approach for workload separation, and encrypted blockstore mapping for regulated workloads.

Attached: blockstore-encryption-matrix.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — encryption options matrix and recommended KMS flow.

High-level ask: please confirm the constraints below so we can lock nodeclass sizing and storage class decisions for the preflight runbook.

Customer constraints we need to confirm:
- Physical segmentation: do tenant boundaries need to align to dedicated racks, or is VLAN-level separation acceptable?
- Storage types allowed: local NVMe, iSCSI LUNs, or LUNs behind a storage gateway? Any NFS disallowed?
- KMS requirements: customer-managed KMS (HSM) vs Redwood-managed with customer key material?
- Network egress policy: is outbound to public internet blocked from compute plane?

Proposed deliverables (next 10 business days):
1) Nodeclass proposal (control, general compute, inference-GPU, storage-proxy) + sizing ranges
2) Storage class mapping and CSI driver recommendation (including encryption, replication scope)
3) Tenant locality mapping guidance (labels, nodeAffinity, and taints)
4) Preflight checklist for ops team (runbook + smoke tests)

Can the Warehouse Systems ops team confirm the three constraints above by EOD Friday? If not, tell us which item to prioritize and we’ll propose a conservative default.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
www.redwoodinference.com

From: Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@warehousesys.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ops Eng <ops@warehousesys.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge-onprem bootstrap: tenant locality, mixed-node profiles & encrypted blockstore plan

Hannah —

Thanks for the draft. Quick answers from our side so you can proceed: 

- Physical segmentation: Tenant boundaries must be rack-aligned for any PCI/PII tenants. Non-regulated tenants can be VLAN-separated.
- Storage types: NVMe (local) preferred for inference cache; block LUNs (iSCSI) are the only allowed remote block devices. NFS is disallowed for regulated tenants.
- KMS: We require customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys; the KMS is reachable over a management VLAN only.
- Network egress: Compute plane cannot reach the public internet directly. Egress must go through a controlled NAT gateway in the DMZ.

Also: SOC2 evidence will be requested during onboarding (logs, KMS access logs, node provisioning records). Our procurement window is tight — we need a working PoC within 6 weeks to meet Q3 commitments.

Janet
Janet Lowe
Head of Infrastructure | Warehouse Systems Inc.
janet.lowe@warehousesys.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@warehousesys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jun 2028 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge-onprem bootstrap: tenant locality, mixed-node profiles & encrypted blockstore plan

Janet — thanks for the quick clarifications. Based on those constraints I sketched a concrete nodeclass and storage mapping. See attached spreadsheet: nodeclass-profile-proposal.xlsx (Excel, 4 sheets).

Summary (high level):
- Nodeclasses
  * control-plane: 3x m5-style control nodes (no GPU), small local SSD for kubelet/containerd, network-only access to KMS over mgmt VLAN.
  * general-compute: 6–12 nodes, CPU optimized for pre/post-processing, uses iSCSI LUNs for persistent workloads.
  * inference-gpu: 2–6 nodes per tenant-rack for initial PoC (A100/80GB or similar), local NVMe for KV cache, encrypted blockstore used for model artifacts via CSI plugin.
  * storage-proxy: 2 nodes (replicated) that present iSCSI LUNs and handle upload/replication to central SAN; reachable from compute via a storage VLAN.

- Storage classes and CSI
  * csi.encrypted-block (RWO): maps to iSCSI LUNs, encryption at rest enforced by customer KMS using provider token exchange flow.
  * local-nvme-cache (RWX/ephemeral): hostPath or local-volume for KV cache — will require eviction policy tuning.
  * object-proxy (external): for model registry uploads to internal object store via storage-proxy nodes.

- Scheduling and locality
  * Use node labels: topology.kubernetes.io/rack=<rack-id> and redwood.tenant=<tenant-id>.
  * Taints on regulated racks: regulated=true:NoSchedule; workload pods for regulated tenants include toleration and nodeAffinity to ensure rack alignment.
  * Admission hook to block pod spec with hostPath unless explicitly allowed (to avoid accidental data bleed).

Open questions for Warehouse Systems:
1) Are we allowed to deploy our kubelet-level metrics collector to the management VLAN, or does it need to be isolated behind an ops jumpbox?
2) Can we run a short-lived privileged init job to pre-provision LVs on the iSCSI LUNs, or do they require manual provisioning by your storage team?

Action items I propose this week:
- Hannah: schedule 60m runbook review with customer ops (include Vivek for network/KMS)
- Lauren: finalize nodeclass spreadsheet and convert nodes -> Terraform module variables
- Laura: assemble SOC2 evidence checklist we can supply within the PoC window

—
Lauren Bishop
Principal Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
nodeclass-profile-proposal.xlsx attached

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Decisions confirmed: 
- Tenant locality: rack-aligned for regulated tenants; VLAN separation allowed for others.
- Storage: local NVMe for cache; iSCSI LUNs for encrypted persistence; no NFS for regulated tenants.
- KMS: customer-managed HSM (management VLAN only).
- Egress: compute -> NAT gateway in DMZ required.

Immediate next steps (owners):
1) Runbook review call — schedule: Friday 2028-06-09 10:00 PT (Hannah / Vivek / Janet). Owner: Hannah.
2) Finalize nodeclass/terraform inputs — owner: Lauren. Deliverable due: 2028-06-12. Attachment: nodeclass-profile-proposal.xlsx
3) SOC2 preflight evidence list — owner: Laura. Deliverable due: 2028-06-12.
4) Blockstore KMS flow diagram (how Redwood will exchange tokens with customer KMS) — owner: Vivek. Deliverable due: 2028-06-12. Attachment referenced: blockstore-encryption-matrix.pdf
